requirements.requirement: Run a RabbitMQ cluster across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmq-server package install completed (INSTALL_DONE) and beam.smp/epmd listening on node1 and node3 (ports 4369/5672/25672 present in after-executor snapshot), but node2's install command was left 'unfinished' with no completion evidence, and no cluster_join/rabbitmqctl join_cluster command was ever run. No evidence of an actual 3-node cluster being formed.

requirements.requirement: Serve AMQP over TLS using a self-created certificate authority
requirements.summary: A CA and per-node certificates were generated on node1 (ca_cert.pem, node1/2/3_cert.pem, verified with openssl verify), but they were never copied to node2/node3, and no rabbitmq.conf/advanced.config enabling ssl_options or a TLS listener (5671) was ever written or applied on any node. The plaintext AMQP port 5672 is the only broker port shown listening in the final snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by the created CA (mutual TLS client authentication)
requirements.summary: A client certificate was generated and verified against the CA, but no RabbitMQ configuration enforcing verify_peer/fail_if_no_peer_cert or any TLS listener was ever applied, so no client-auth enforcement exists in the captured evidence.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: The management plugin was never enabled and no port 15672 appears in any after-executor listening-socket snapshot, so there is no management interface to restrict, and no firewall/bind-address configuration was applied.

overall_summary: The executor spent its entire 2100-second budget fighting apt/dpkg lock contention and unreliable upstream package mirrors, and the run terminated on a timeout before any RabbitMQ cluster, TLS, client-certificate enforcement, or management-interface restriction was configured. rabbitmq-server was installed on node1 and node3 (confirmed via INSTALL_DONE and listening beam.smp/epmd sockets in the final snapshot) but node2's install was left in-flight and unconfirmed. A CA and node/client certificates were generated on node1 only, verified locally, but never distributed or wired into RabbitMQ configuration on any node — no TLS listener, no client-cert enforcement, and no management plugin was ever enabled. The run also left node2 and node3 with ssh.service in a failed state that did not exist before the run, alongside abandoned apt-source edits and stray temp files.
limitations: No rabbitmqctl status, cluster_status, or cluster join commands were captured, so cluster formation cannot be confirmed or ruled out beyond the absence of evidence.
node2's rabbitmq-server install completion was never confirmed (final command timeline entry is 'unfinished'), leaving its package/service state indeterminate.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (pre/post boot-identity around a restart) was not present in the captured evidence at all — no restart was performed or observed on any node, so availability/recovery behavior cannot be assessed.

The root cause of the new ssh.service/ssh.socket failed state on node2/node3 is not directly evidenced in the command trace; it appears correlated with the failed cross-node SSH setup attempt but a definitive causal link could not be established from the captured commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: The run left node2 and node3 with ssh.service/ssh.socket in a failed state that was not present before-prepare (a regression visible in after_executor vs before_prepare comparison), and this was never diagnosed or fixed. Numerous unnecessary/abandoned mutations accumulated: repeated background 'nohup apt-get' launches that collided with each other and had to be killed with 'sudo kill -9' and forcible removal of dpkg/apt lock files (cmd-f0e200dc67df4437, cmd-6aeb03f0b4344cc2, cmd-6ec24626b7f74c90, cmd-5bc72a0dfb73461c, cmd-950b45bef37442f8), a bad empty rabbitmq.gpg keyring file created and later removed, an rabbitmq.list apt source file that was written, edited (sed replacing hostname), then deleted entirely without ever being reinstated for the final approach, and stray files left in /tmp (apt1.log, apt2.log, nohup1-3.log, rmqinstall.log, test.key) that were never cleaned up. The CA/cert material generated in ~/rabbitmq-ca on node1 was never propagated or used, effectively abandoned residue. An attempted SSH key/authorized_keys write for cross-node access (cmd-edcb53179e9f4f39) also failed and was not followed up or reverted.
